minutes.headline: Board recommended six warrant articles, deferred five, and removed the old primary school and Community Preservation articles.
minutes.summary: The board voted to sign a final bond for pavement management and the middle/high school project. It then took recommendation votes on the remaining annual Town Meeting warrant articles and approved the FY2021 budget recommendation. The streetlight purchase drew the longest debate and was deferred to Town Meeting. The board also discussed the town manager's role in school bargaining, hunting near conservation land, and Town Meeting COVID planning.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-0 on roll call to adopt the bond vote for the final borrowing for pavement management and the middle/high school project.
The board recommended the capital plan as presented (3-1, one abstention) and recommended the FY2021 budget as presented, with one member opposed.
The board removed the old primary school article from the warrant 3-2, and later removed the Community Preservation Act article.
The board deferred the streetlight purchase, the sewer enterprise fund, earth removal changes and liquor license petition articles to Town Meeting.
The board signed the annual Town Meeting and election warrant, and asked that Town Meeting pandemic planning go on next week's agenda.

why_it_matters: The capital plan is funded fully by free cash, so the recommended projects and the streetlight purchase compete for the same unappropriated money rather than new taxes, and residents will vote on them at Town Meeting.
Articles that were deferred have no board recommendation yet, and the removed old primary school and Community Preservation articles will not be on the Town Meeting warrant.
watch_next: Next week's Select Board agenda: planning for holding Town Meeting safely during the pandemic, and the pledge of allegiance.
Board recommendations at Town Meeting on the deferred articles, including streetlights and earth removal article BB after its presentation.
